dossier.architecture: Very low stow, full-width protected intake and four-roller cannon; endgame added around the core scorer.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom swerve top plates allow shooter stow between modules, below one foot per team interview.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper intake; powered centering wheels added before Worlds.
subsystems.transfer: Intake/trigger transmission remains concentric with the shooter pivot, permitting feeding at many angles.
subsystems.scoring: Four horizontal contact rollers stabilize a narrowed note. Rack-and-pinion pivot draws inspiration from 971's 2017 turret.
subsystems.endgame: Light hook-deploy linkage, winches and passive spring/servo trap-door fingers reuse the main shooter.
subsystems.controls: Fast sensor loop, slip/collision-aware localization, note-search auto recovery, tilt/roll-aware climb coordination.

versions: Rubber coating ballooned at speed; switched to vulcanized rollers. Trapped notes caused two losses; added a servo-raised deflector. Centering wheels added before Champs.
dossier.analysis: This is an explicit hierarchy: protect speaker/amp cycle performance first and fit climbing/trap around it. The compact package succeeds because the controls handle narrowed-note flight and changing robot pose. New 1833 design-transfer study: docs/context/1833-reference-2024-1690.md. Historical success does not waive the current no-support/no-turret mandate or certify causal performance.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.

context_documents.title: 2024-1690 · A small robot still needs protection against rare disabling note poses
context_documents.body:
> Physical evidence update 2026-11-07: read the complete [upgrade report](../PHYSICAL_UPGRADE_REPORT.md) and the new physical studies in `data/physical_studies.jsonl`. Earlier source accounts below retain their publication scopes.

# 2024-1690: A small robot still needs protection against rare disabling note poses

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A compact custom-swerve robot feeds its launcher through pivot-concentric transmission elements. The retained launcher uses four horizontal contacts and a rack-based angle mechanism. A note deflector was added before championships after notes lodged beneath the shooter in two losses; the climb controller corrects roll and coordinates trap release with swing.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly contrasts the season’s small/simple objective with the prior year’s complexity. The deflector is a response to two specific disabling events, not a decorative cover.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Rare jams can dominate an otherwise excellent scoring architecture because they remove the whole robot’s contribution. Preventing entry to a bad configuration can be more reliable than detecting and reversing it later. Concentric feeding preserves operation across launcher angles, but actual clearances and moving power transmission still need review. Trap timing based on swing is a separate dynamic-control problem, not proof of static shot accuracy.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Reproduce the reported under-shooter trap pose, test the deflector with damaged notes, and validate swing/roll compensation under asymmetric chain capture.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/jB7OqueRYf0](https://youtu.be/jB7OqueRYf0)

context_documents.title: 2024-1690 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
context_documents.body:
## 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development

Primary facts: the reveal gives an approximately 11-inch highest stowed point. Official results identify Orbit as a 2024 world champion. The mechanism is chassis-yaw aimed; its elevation/pivot motion is not a turret. In the CAD release, a team member warns that low packaging did not make every individual mechanism superior and that substantial work was needed. The team's controls explanation describes physically limited motion commands, skid/collision handling, driver assistance and automated shot readiness. Treat this as a team account rather than an independent performance decomposition.

1833 transfer analysis: low CG can increase usable acceleration and reduce settling, but free speed or stowed height alone cannot predict cycles. Compare time to accelerate, brake, reacquire heading, capture a piece and release a valid shot under contact. The cost of chassis aiming must be included in a non-turret architecture's state model. It may be small when acquisition exits with a useful heading and the driver can approach efficiently; it may be large when position and heading are constrained together. Geometry and software must be co-designed so that the driver requests remain physically feasible.

This example validates ambition with a compact architecture. It does not justify eliminating a necessary game function, assuming development is easy, or concluding that the lowest robot always wins. A low package that creates rare disabling piece poses may lose more match contribution than it gains in an ideal cycle. Preserve the existing note-deflector study as a reliability problem alongside the positive architecture example. The future design should carry an explicit optimization budget: time for loaded tuning, autonomous coordination, repeated defended acquisition, operator feedback and service drills. Hardware simplicity buys development capacity only if the saved effort is actually invested in those areas.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350 (post 8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838 (post 7); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350/142 ; https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2024/CMPTX/awards ; existing `docs/research_continuation/2024-1690.md`. No new CAD-dimensional certification.

context_documents.title: 2024-1690 physical construction / interfaces / transfer
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1690: Doppler CAD release and retained interview

Generated from `data/physical_studies.jsonl`; edit that authoritative record.

## Whole robot and packaging

Four corner drive modules surround a very low transport and launcher assembly. The inspected CAD screenshot shows wide transverse rollers and launcher motors packed into the central space between modules. The launcher changes elevation instead of yawing independently of the chassis. Its feed transmission is organized around the elevation pivot so a ring can pass into the launcher across its angle range. A raised climb/trap pose shown in another source image is not the everyday driving envelope. Battery location and removal path cannot be established from these images, and are deliberately omitted from the layout.

## Piece flow

A floor note reaches the pickup mouth and is pulled inward while lying approximately flat. Rollers move it through the low transport path to the pivot-related feed region. Launcher contacts then accelerate and release it at the selected elevation. A later deflector keeps a note from entering the space under the shooter. That deflector prevents an unwanted alternative route; it is not another powered feed stage. Climb/trap operation reuses moving hardware but introduces a separate lifted geometry and dynamic timing problem.

## Annotated views

Editorial reconstruction. Not to scale; only explicit dimension labels are source dimensions. No CAD-derived measurements. Dashed envelopes are schematic and not clearance certification.

![physical-2024-1690-top](../../images/physical/physical-2024-1690-top.png)

![physical-2024-1690-side](../../images/physical/physical-2024-1690-side.png)

![physical-2024-1690-transition](../../images/physical/physical-2024-1690-transition.png)

## Compact intake and pivot-related transport

### Published construction

The retained interview describes pivot-concentric transmission elements; the inspected overhead CAD view shows the closely packed central rollers and motors.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

The note must remain held while its center passes from the low pickup into the launcher. Pivoting changes the location of the launcher relative to fixed structure; the feed must continue to bridge that gap.

### Engineering interpretation

Concentric power routing can keep belt-center relationships stable while a launcher pivots. It does not alone prove the note remains constrained. That requires actual overlap of driving and supporting contacts through the worst angle.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

Borrow the pivot-related routing principle; retain actual support across the moving handoff. Low height alone does not demonstrate easy packaging or manufacturing.

### Unknowns

Exact roller diameters, note compression, trigger sensing and feed overlap through the full angle range remain unknown.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

## Horizontal contacts and rack-based elevation

### Published construction

The retained study describes four horizontal launcher contacts and rack angle actuation. The team CAD-release reply explains pinions made from two plates with steel pins acting as teeth.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

The launcher is brought to the intended elevation before feeding. The contacts accelerate the note; chassis heading supplies azimuth. A feed pause while aiming is normal operation, not automatically a jam.

### Engineering interpretation

A lantern-style pinion can be manufactured from plates and pins, but tooth contact, backlash and rack support remain output-angle error sources. Compactness trades away some shot range and individual mechanism advantages according to the team discussion.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

Electric elevation and chassis aim suit current constraints. Replicate only after checking the contact and bearing load path; do not borrow an unspecified gear ratio.

### Unknowns

The new review did not measure rack geometry, output stiffness or competition speed. No released control binary is certified.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

### Published construction

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

A loose or badly oriented note is blocked from entering the dead space. It must remain outside or return to the intended pickup path instead of becoming trapped under moving shooter hardware.

A guard is valuable because it removes a bad configuration, not because it adds another command. It must clear the launcher sweep, drive module steering, and legitimate note path.

A low scoring package may still require demanding endgame control. Source opinions differ about whether trap pursuit was the best compromise; preserve those as individual assessments.

physical_studies.version_label: Doppler CAD release and retained interview
physical_studies.packaging: Four corner drive modules surround a very low transport and launcher assembly. The inspected CAD screenshot shows wide transverse rollers and launcher motors packed into the central space between modules. The launcher changes elevation instead of yawing independently of the chassis. Its feed transmission is organized around the elevation pivot so a ring can pass into the launcher across its angle range. A raised climb/trap pose shown in another source image is not the everyday driving envelope. Battery location and removal path cannot be established from these images, and are deliberately omitted from the layout.
physical_studies.piece_flow: A floor note reaches the pickup mouth and is pulled inward while lying approximately flat. Rollers move it through the low transport path to the pivot-related feed region. Launcher contacts then accelerate and release it at the selected elevation. A later deflector keeps a note from entering the space under the shooter. That deflector prevents an unwanted alternative route; it is not another powered feed stage. Climb/trap operation reuses moving hardware but introduces a separate lifted geometry and dynamic timing problem.

mechanisms.title: Compact intake and pivot-related transport
mechanisms.construction: The retained interview describes pivot-concentric transmission elements; the inspected overhead CAD view shows the closely packed central rollers and motors.
mechanisms.operating_sequence: The note must remain held while its center passes from the low pickup into the launcher. Pivoting changes the location of the launcher relative to fixed structure; the feed must continue to bridge that gap.
mechanisms.engineering_interpretation: Concentric power routing can keep belt-center relationships stable while a launcher pivots. It does not alone prove the note remains constrained. That requires actual overlap of driving and supporting contacts through the worst angle.
mechanisms.unknowns: Exact roller diameters, note compression, trigger sensing and feed overlap through the full angle range remain unknown.
mechanisms.team_stated_rationale: Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.
mechanisms.transfer: Borrow the pivot-related routing principle; retain actual support across the moving handoff. Low height alone does not demonstrate easy packaging or manufacturing.

mechanisms.title: Horizontal contacts and rack-based elevation

source_reviews.title: Orbit releases Doppler CAD
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team release and technical response
facts: Orbit released CAD for Doppler. The team emphasized its low height and described tradeoffs against other robots' intake, shooter, amp and trap concepts.
source_reviews.limitations: Team comparison is qualitative. It does not establish outcomes under a common test.

source_reviews.title: Orbit CAD technical replies
source_reviews.locator: Posts on lower kicker, pass control, service joint and arm homing
facts: Orbit says a lower roller lifts the note first. Top-first compression tended to drag the note on carpet and draw more current in testing.
Field location selects one of two preset passing angles. The compact pivot uses relative motor sensing and a closed-position Hall check at startup.
Interlocking shooter mount features add rigidity for service. The complete shooter still requires removal of a belt-coupled shaft.
source_reviews.limitations: No current traces or fixture measurements. No CAD geometry or full video captions re-read.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Doppler prioritized a very low travel profile. The robot therefore had to acquire a flat, compliant ring without pinning it to the carpet, guide it through a constrained path and aim by moving the shooter in pitch and the chassis in yaw. Orbit's technical answers identify a specific acquisition choice that helped. The bottom roller made the first contact and lifted the note into the next contacts. The compact package also drove a sensing compromise at the arm pivot and a mechanical joint intended to preserve stiffness while permitting removal.
piece_flow: The bottom roller catches the approaching rim and lifts it into the feed. The alternative top-first pinch caused carpet drag in the team's tests.
The inherited record routes the note into the pivoted launcher and alternate placement functions. The exact contact sequence beyond acquisition was outside the reviewed replies.
The public answer identifies separate flat and high passing trajectories selected using field position. This describes passing modes, distinct from the normal speaker calibration.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A low robot can preserve a route under the stage, but the usable space between carpet, bumper, first roller and electronics is small. That makes the leading contact, suspension deflection and service stack-up critical. The pivot is compact enough that Orbit chose a Hall reference at its closed position instead of an absolute angle sensor. Two travel barriers physically support the shooter near its edges in the team explanation.

subsystems.name: Bottom-first floor pickup
subsystems.construction: A low leading roller encounters the note before the upper roller can pinch it against carpet.
subsystems.operation: Kick the rim upward and immediately capture it with the rest of the intake.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reported less carpet drag, lower current and favorable capture compared with its top-compression trial.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The roller must apply enough upward impulse for the next contact to take over without pushing the note ahead. Required grip and surface speed will depend on note stiffness and vehicle speed.
subsystems.interfaces: Carpet, bumper lip, note edge, lower roller and second contact define the capture envelope.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare current and successful capture across approach speed and worn notes. Watch first contact in slow motion after a bracket replacement.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual operating clearances and current distribution.

subsystems.name: Pivot, aiming and homing
subsystems.construction: Compact shooter pivot with relative motor feedback, closed-position Hall sensor and mechanical travel supports.
subsystems.operation: Start from a known closed condition. Aim the chassis and set pitch for the shot. Select a preset passing pitch from field position.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team cited space as the reason for omitting an absolute sensor at that pivot.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An at-home check can be robust while adding an operational dependency after a reset. A robot disabled mid-travel needs a way to restore the datum without forcing the arm against an obstacle.
subsystems.interfaces: Pivot stops, hall alignment, pass zones and chassis aim.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Reboot at home, off home and after a Hall bracket shift. Verify the fault and recovery path independently.
subsystems.unknowns: Angle tolerances, deployed event code and handoff alignment.

subsystems.name: Launcher mounting and service
subsystems.construction: Interlocking plates and clamshell around blocks supporting the main shaft. A belt still couples a shaft to the assembly.
subsystems.operation: Keep the joint rigid in operation and separate the launcher for service.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team explained that interlocking profiles stiffen the attachment compared with relying on screws alone.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The service gain depends on actual extraction order and whether the locating faces wear. Measure return to aim datum after multiple swaps.
subsystems.interfaces: Shaft removal, belt release, wiring and tool access all affect the real service time.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Practice removal and calibrate after reassembly. Inspect locator faces for trapped debris or impact wear.
subsystems.unknowns: Fit specification, assembly time and repeatability data.

revisions: Team describes top-first ground compression as a tested alternative and the lower kicker as the adopted approach. Detailed competition revision boundaries remain in the older dossier.
transferable_principles: For a sliding ring, test the initial contact direction before specifying more ground compression. Verify power loss and restart for any compact mechanism that uses relative position sensing.
disconfirming_conditions: A bottom-first roller can fail if it throws pieces forward or if the next contact cannot take them in before the chassis overtakes them. Extreme low packaging loses value if clearance or recovery degrades primary cycles.
remaining_gaps: Event-specific full-path release drawings, measured pickup current and accuracy, full captions and installed arm recovery behavior.
